source.title: Pioneering Precision in Lumbar Spine MRI Segmentation with Advanced Deep Learning and Data Enhancement
source.authors: Istiak Ahmed; Md. Tanzim Hossain; M. Nahid; Kazi Shahriar Sanjid; M. Junayed; M. M. Uddin; Mohammad Monirujjaman Khan

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training results for a modified U-Net on MRI segmentation, but does not measure training classification error on CIFAR or the claim versions' stated benchmarks and interventions.
record.gate_note: The study reports training and validation curves for accuracy, Dice coefficient, and Mean IoU over 100 epochs, but supplies no numerical training classification error. Rows record the reported accuracy curve result and the separate dataset-specific segmentation metrics; cited findings are not included.
record.test_reason: The study uses Glorot initialization and batch normalization in an MRI segmentation model and reports its performance. It provides no initialization, normalization, depth, width, or learning-rate comparison testing V1–V6. Training curves without readable numerical training error do not establish V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: they attribute improved lumbar-spine segmentation and handling of class imbalance to preprocessing, the modified U-Net, and combined focal and Dice loss. Their claim of superiority across all metrics overstates Table 3, where spinal-canal detection is tied at 100%. The study does not isolate the contributions of initialization, batch normalization, or individual architectural changes.
record.recipe_differences: Medical image segmentation on SPIDER-derived lumbar MRI, using a modified U-Net with leaky ReLU, Glorot uniform initialization, and combined focal and Dice loss; not a CIFAR classification or claim-version comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and anatomical class vary in Table 2; reported segmentation metric values differ across them.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed model reports high class-wise segmentation scores across T1, T2, and T2 SPACE images. Table 3 reports higher Dice and lower ASD than nn-UNET, with equal spinal-canal detection.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed preprocessing and modified U-Net pipeline achieves the reported lumbar MRI segmentation performance.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report that training and validation accuracy, Dice, and Mean IoU curves nearly overlap after 100 epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: This segmentation model has similar reported training and validation metrics after 100 epochs.

record.problems: The paper provides no numerical training accuracy or training classification error in the text. Accuracy, Dice, and Mean IoU curves are figure-only, and no uncertainty estimates are reported. Its task is medical-image segmentation rather than the classification settings in the listed versions.
record.rows_left_out: None. The training curves for Dice and Mean IoU are described alongside Figure 12 but remain figure-only and do not measure any listed version; the per-class table values and the reported comparator entries are retained.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, and effects of size, early stopping, or regularization.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training degradation with depth, identity residual shortcuts, very deep plain tanh networks, and Fixup.
Effects of initialization on training speed, signal and gradient propagation, and trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature changes, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Glorot initialization and batch normalization are recipe components, not experimentally tested interventions here. Section 4 cites Santurkar et al., an original V6 source, but supplies no normalization ablation. All row states refer to whether the measures establish a listed version, not whether the reported segmentation scores exist.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification, random or corrupted labels, model size effects, and near-zero training classification error are not tested.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and width differences are not tested.
Plain versus residual depth comparisons and the cited ImageNet/CIFAR settings are not tested.
Initialization comparisons, signal or gradient propagation, and trainable depth are not tested.
Learning-rate stability, curvature, sharpness, and divergence are not tested.
Batch-normalization ablations, training speed comparisons, and learning-rate tolerance comparisons are not tested.

rows.stage_stated: trained on SPIDER-derived lumbar spine MRI images
rows.operation_detail: Trained for 100 epochs with batch size 8; evaluated with training and validation accuracy curves.
rows.measure: Training accuracy over epochs
rows.note: The text says Figures 12–14 show accuracy, Dice coefficient, and Mean IoU over 100 epochs, and that training and validation curves almost overlap after 100 epochs. No numerical training accuracy is given in the text.
rows.check: The supplied text contains the figure caption and qualitative curve description, but no readable training accuracy values. Curve overlap does not establish near-zero training classification error or any other version.
